newsitem.title: CUBA: France boosts export credits to Cuba.
newsitem.headline: France boosts export credits to Cuba.

text.p: France boosted export credits to Cuba to some $175 million this year, up from $155 million in 1996, France's ambassador Jean-Raphael Dufour said Thursday in Havana.
Dufour cited the sum to reporters after signing an accord to disburse the third and final tranche of a $6 million grant to upgrade Cuban electrical power plants.
The grant is earmarked to provide technology to aid Cuban plants to use heavier-grade domestic Cuban oil rather than foreign crude.
Dufour also announced France was about to donate some $2 million worth of wheat and wheat flour to the island.
The ambassador did not specify when Paris raised the export credit level.
But he added Paris'recently-increased export credits are backed, in turn, by guaranteed Cuban sugar exports to France.
Havana drew on export credits mostly for food imports like wheat, the envoy said.
Bilateral trade between France and Cuba was about $200 in 1996, officials said.
French investment on the island includes oil exploration ventures and tourism, and French firms have also financed Cuban sugar production
Cuba's official bilateral debt to France amounts to about $450 million, excluding commercial loans.

Communist-ruled Cuba, strapped for access to loans other than short-term and expensive commercial credit, must grapple with a trade deficit that grew to an estimated $1.7 billion in 1996, up from $1.2 billion in 1995.
